eyebrow: XYZ LAYOUT ENGINE · VISUAL ARCHITECTURE & EDITING GUIDE
title: HOW A POSTER IS ASSEMBLED
subtitle: From JSON content, transparent PNG assets, and a Node.js recipe to self-contained HTML and raster PNG

headline.caption: Edit sections.header.headline in the JSON fixture (nutrition/fixture.json) to change the poster headline words without touching layout code.

artwork.caption: Choose artwork by changing hero.illustrationId ("leaf_glow") or swapping leaf_glow.png to replace the hero leaf illustration.

placement.caption: Adjust hero leaf placement in nutrition.mjs: left 262 shifts x-offset, top -34 pulls it 34px up, width 428 and height 640 resize its box.

assembly.heading: EXPLODED 3D SCENE LAYERS · 1000 × 1000 COORDINATE SPACE
assembly.note: Flexbox rows frame an open center window on L4 while the hero leaf floats independently on L3 at absolute coordinates (left: 262, top: -34).

viewer.heading: ASSEMBLED POSTER & VIEWER EXPERIENCE
viewer.caption: Either backend exports self-contained offline HTML (render-inline.html) with live selectable text, versus flat pixels in an exported PNG.

pipeline.heading: ENGINE RENDER PIPELINE · WHEN JS RUNS, WHAT CSS DOES & WHERE BACKENDS FIT

nodeRecipe.caption: At render time, the JavaScript recipe (source/nutrition.mjs) executes in the Node.js runtime to validate inputs, fit text, and build the scene.

cssStyling.caption: toDocument() serializes scene style properties into inline CSS styling and embedded @font-face rules so CSS handles all HTML layout.

satoriSvg.caption: Vector path: Satori computes Flexbox layout in Node.js with bundled fonts and renders the scene tree into standalone SVG markup.

resvgPng.caption: Raster step: resvg (@resvg/resvg-js) rasterizes Satori's SVG vector output directly into a finished PNG image (render.png).

playwrightChromium.caption: Browser path: Playwright drives headless Chromium to load the self-contained HTML and compute exact CSS layout and font metrics.

chromiumCapture.caption: Screenshot step: Chromium performs PNG capture via page.screenshot() to export the rendered viewport as render.png.
